primary.title: Apology
primary.author: Plato
primary.rationale: Plato's account of Socrates' defense at his trial. Considered a foundational text for understanding Socrates' philosophy and character.

primary.title: Crito
primary.author: Plato
primary.rationale: A dialogue between Socrates and Crito discussing justice and the citizen's duty to the state, set during Socrates' imprisonment.

primary.title: Phaedo
primary.author: Plato
primary.rationale: Recounts Socrates' final hours and his philosophical discussions on the immortality of the soul.

secondary.title: Socrates: A Very Short Introduction
secondary.author: C.C.W. Taylor
secondary.rationale: A concise and accessible scholarly introduction to Socrates' life, thought, and the Socratic problem, by a leading scholar.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Socrates
secondary.author: Donald R. Morrison
secondary.rationale: A collection of essays by prominent scholars covering various aspects of Socrates' philosophy, historical context, and influence.

secondary.title: Socrates and the Jews: Test Cases
secondary.author: Leo Strauss
secondary.rationale: While published in 1976, this work by a highly influential political philosopher offers a unique perspective on Socrates' philosophical method and its implications.

suggestions.notes: Socrates himself wrote nothing. Our knowledge of him comes primarily through the writings of his students, most notably Plato and Xenophon. The 'primary sources' listed are therefore Plato's dialogues, which are widely considered the most reliable, though still filtered through Plato's own philosophical agenda.
